```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(performance)
library(vegan)
library(emmeans)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom.mixed)
library(tidyverse)

annot_master<-read.csv(here("Data", "cluster_and_ed50_data.csv")) #from phenotype_heatmap script
df_modeling <- annot_master %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("K_"), site), as.factor)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ED50), !is.na(site))

k_cols <- paste0("K_", 2:15)
```

```{r}
library(purrr)

# 1. Create a named list of all your model objects
all_models <- list(
  "spp_m" = spp_m,
  "k2m"   = k2m,   "k2ms"  = k2ms,
  "k3m"   = k3m,   "k3ms"  = k3ms,
  "k4m"   = k4m,   "k4ms"  = k4ms,
  "k5m"   = k5m,   "k5ms"  = km5s, 
  "k6m"   = k6m,   "k6ms"  = k6ms,
  "k7m"   = k7m,   "k7ms"  = k7ms,
  "k8m"   = k8m,   "k8ms"  = k8ms,
  "k9m"   = k9m,   "k9ms"  = k9ms,
  "k10m"  = k10m,  "k10ms" = k10ms,
  "k11m"  = k11m,  "k11ms" = k11ms,
  "k12m"  = k12m,  "k12ms" = k12ms,
  "k13m"  = k13m,  "k13ms" = k13ms,
  "k14m"  = k14m,  "k14ms" = k14ms
)

# 2. Extract AIC, BIC, and both R2 values together
master_model_table <- imap_dfr(all_models, function(model_obj, model_name) {
  
  # Grab information criteria
  perf <- model_performance(model_obj)
  
  # Grab variance partition metrics
  r2_vals <- r2(model_obj)
  
  data.frame(
    Model_Name      = model_name,
    AIC             = round(perf$AIC, 1),
    BIC             = round(perf$BIC, 1),
    Marginal_R2     = round(r2_vals$R2_marginal, 3),
    Conditional_R2  = round(r2_vals$R2_conditional, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

# 3. View the table sorted by AIC to look at the trade-offs cleanly
print(master_model_table %>% arrange(AIC))


write.csv(master_model_table, here("Data", "master_model_table.csv"))

top_models <- list(
  "K3_plus_Spp"  = k3ms,
  "K4_plus_Spp"  = k4ms,
  "Just_Spp" = spp_m
)

anova_table <- lapply(names(top_models), function(model_name) {
  m <- top_models[[model_name]]
  an <- anova(m)
  
  as.data.frame(an) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    mutate(Model = model_name)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(Model, term, everything()) # Keeps it scannable

print(anova_table)

var_table <- imap_dfr(top_models, function(m, model_name) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  
  # Extract site variance safely
  site_var <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "site"] 
  if(length(site_var) == 0) site_var <- 0 # Fallback safety if variance is exactly 0
  
  # Extract residual variance
  resid_var <- attr(VarCorr(m), "sc")^2
  total <- site_var + resid_var
  
  tibble(
    Model             = model_name,
    Site_variance     = site_var,
    Residual_variance = resid_var,
    Site_prop         = site_var / total,
    Residual_prop     = resid_var / total
  )
})

print(var_table)

emmeans_table <- imap_dfr(top_3_models, function(m, model_name) {
  # Calculate post-hoc differences between your species lines
  em <- emmeans(m, ~ species)
  
  tidy(pairs(em)) %>%
    mutate(Model = model_name)
})

print(emmeans_table)
```

```{r}
# Loop through and compute AIC using lmer()
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(lme4)
library(performance)

model_comp <- map_df(k_cols, function(k_name) {
  
  # Fit the model (REML = FALSE is mandatory for comparing fixed structures via AIC)
  form <- as.formula(paste("ED50 ~ species +", k_name, "+ (1 | site)"))
  model <- lmer(form, data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
  
  # Grab AIC and BIC
  perf <- model_performance(model)
  
  data.frame(
    Model          = k_name,
    AIC            = perf$AIC,
    BIC            = perf$BIC,           # Punishes overfitting harder than AIC
    R2_Marginal    = perf$R2_marginal,    # Variance explained by Species + K-Cluster
    R2_Conditional = perf$R2_conditional  # Total variance explained including Site
  )
})

# Arrange by best AIC to see the trade-offs
print(model_comp %>% arrange(AIC))

# 1. Fit the final, optimal model structure
final_model <- lmer(ED50 ~ species + K_3 + (1 | site), 
                    data = df_modeling, 
                    REML = TRUE)

# 2. Look at the coefficients to see WHICH clusters are more tolerant
summary(final_model)

# 3. Check exactly how much heat tolerance separates the groups (in degrees C)
tidy(k2ms, effects = "fixed")

table(df_modeling$species, df_modeling$K_3)
```

```{r}
#plot ED50 by cluster assignment, here K=3
#ordering by host 
#custom_order <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "10", "11", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9", "12")
custom_order <- c("1", "3", "2") #make plot then change these if needed

# --- 2. Clean Data & Reorder Factor Levels ---
df_sorted <- df_modeling %>%
  mutate(
    #enter the K here (i.e. K_) to follow your specific sequence on the x-axis
    K_sorted = factor(as.character(K_3), levels = custom_order),
    species_color = toupper(trimws(species))
  ) %>%
  # Drop any rows that don't match your custom level list (if any exist)
  filter(!is.na(K_sorted))

# --- 3. Build the Single Unfaceted Plot ---
ggplot(df_sorted, aes(x = K_sorted, y = ED50)) +
  # One clean boxplot per cluster step along your custom x-axis order
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA, color = "black", fill = "grey98") +
  
  # Scatter individual dots colored by species
  geom_jitter(aes(color = species_color, shape = site), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
   # title = "ED50 Phenotypes Ordered by Custom Cluster Sequence",
    x = "K Cluster Assignment",
    y = expression(ED[50]*" Score"),
    color = "Species"
  ) #K=4, groups 1 and 2 are different. p =0.009
#k=11, group 5 is different from 1 3 and 4

# Save the plot with a wide canvas ratio to accommodate the 12 columns
#ggsave(here("Plots", "ED50_K12_boxplot_Sorted.png"), plot = plot_sorted_k12, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
#plot predictions

# 1. Extract predictions (fitted values) from your final model
df_modeling$Predicted_ED50 <- predict(final_model)

# 2. Plot Raw vs. Predicted
plot_pred_vs_raw <- ggplot(df_modeling, aes(x = Predicted_ED50, y = ED50)) +
  # Add a 1:1 line. If predictions were perfect, dots would sit exactly on this line
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Scatter dots colored by Species and shaped by Cluster Group
  geom_point(aes(color = toupper(species), shape = as.factor(K_3)), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Add a trend line of your actual fit to see deviation from the 1:1 line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "darkblue", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Model Validation: Predicted vs. Observed Heat Tolerance",
    subtitle = "Dashed Line = Perfect 1:1 Prediction | Solid Line = Actual Model Fit",
    x = expression("Predicted " * ED[50] * " (°C)"),
    y = expression("Observed Raw " * ED[50] * " (°C)"),
    color = "Species",
    shape = "K_3 Cluster"
  )

# Display the plot
print(plot_pred_vs_raw)

# Save to your plots directory
ggsave(here("Plots", "ED50_Predicted_vs_Raw.png"), plot = plot_pred_vs_raw, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```


```{r}
r2_vals <- model_performance(model)

test_residuals <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = model)
plot(test_residuals)

k3_m <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_3 + species + (1 | site), data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
k10_m <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_10 + species + (1 | site), data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
k8_m  <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_8 + species + (1 | site),  data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)

# 2. Run the comparative ANOVA (Likelihood Ratio Test)
anova(k3_m, k10_m, k8_m)
#10 is lowest aic when 
summary(k11_m)
summary(k12_m)
summary(k4_m)

r2(k11_m) #conditional () = 0.514, marginal (sites) = 0.242. So, fixed effect explains 17% of variance, site explains 22.5% (39.4-16.9)
r2(k12_m) #conditional () = 0.395, marginal () = 0.170
r2(k4_m) #conditional () = 0.379, marginal () = 0.087
# 1. Calculate the estimated marginal means for each cluster group
k11_means <- emmeans(k11_m, specs = ~ K_11)


# 2. Run the pairwise post-hoc comparisons with Tukey adjustment
k11_posthoc <- pairs(k11_means, adjust = "tukey")

# 3. View the results
# (Optional: filter for only statistically significant differences)
k11_posthoc_df <- as.data.frame(k11_posthoc)

significant_differences <- k11_posthoc_df %>% 
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

print(significant_differences)
pairs(emmeans(k11_m, ~ K_11))
plot(k11_means, comparisons = TRUE)

# Plot residuals against fitted values
plot(k11_m, type = c("p", "smooth"), 
     xlab = "Fitted Values (Predicted ED50)", 
     ylab = "Residuals")

res <- residuals(k11_m)

# Create Q-Q plot
qqnorm(res, main = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals")

custom_order <- c("1", "2", "3", "4",  "9", "7","10", "11", "5", "6",  "8") #make plot then change these if needed

#change order
df_modeling$K_11 <- factor(df_modeling$K_11, levels = custom_order)

# 2. Re-run emmeans (it will automatically adopt the new factor order)
k11_predicted <- as.data.frame(emmeans(k11_m, ~ K_11))


# 2. Plot raw data as points, and model predictions as larger points with error bars
ggplot() +
  # Raw data points (colored by site to see the random effect)
  geom_jitter(data = df_modeling, aes(x = K_11, y = ED50, color = species, shape = site), alpha = 0.5, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  # Model predictions (Emmeans)
  geom_point(data = k11_predicted, aes(x = K_11, y = emmean), size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(data = k11_predicted, aes(x = K_11, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), 
                color = "black", width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Model Fit: Raw ED50 Data vs. Model Predictions",
       x = "K_11 Category",
       y = "ED50")
```
